name: Kang-Petrov Arms KPS-12 'Workbench'
description:
The Kang-Petrov KPS-12 is a pump-action shotgun chambered in 12 gauge with a six-round tubular magazine and an 18.5-inch barrel. It is the shotgun equivalent of the KP-19 pistol — reliable, affordable, available everywhere, and remarkable only for its unremarkable competence. The receiver is machined aluminum, the barrel is chrome-lined, and the furniture is black synthetic polymer that resists damage from the environments where the weapon is commonly deployed.

The Workbench is the most widely deployed security shotgun in GLMZ. Kang-Petrov's volume pricing makes it the default choice for security firms equipping large teams, and the weapon's durability means they rarely need replacing. Racks of KPS-12s line the armories of building security offices, facility defense teams, and checkpoint operators throughout the Mids. The chrome-lined barrel maintains accuracy even after thousands of rounds, and the pump action continues to cycle after years of minimal maintenance.

Kang-Petrov sells the Workbench in cases of six, with volume discounts that make bulk purchasing irresistible for security firms. The company also offers an armorer's maintenance kit and a training program for security personnel — a complete package that has made the KPS-12 the institutional shotgun of choice.

caliber: 12 gauge

rate_of_fire: Pump-action
magazine_capacity: 6+1 rounds
weight: 3.0 kg
tactical_use: A reliable pump-action shotgun for institutional security use. The chrome-lined barrel maintains accuracy over extended service life. The pump action provides consistent cycling regardless of ammunition type. Suitable for building security, checkpoint operations, and general defensive duties. Capacity and reloading speed are adequate for most security scenarios.
cultural_context: The Workbench is the wallpaper of GLMZ's security infrastructure — so ubiquitous that most people don't notice it anymore. Security guards carry them, checkpoints display them, and building lobbies rack them behind glass marked 'emergency.' The KPS-12 is not a weapon that inspires conversation. It is a weapon that fills a rack and waits.
story_hooks: A serial number analysis reveals that KPS-12s from a specific production batch are appearing in both legitimate security armories and Shelf criminal arsenals — someone in the distribution chain is duplicating shipments.
A security guard's Workbench is loaded with dragon's breath incendiary rounds during what should have been a routine riot-control deployment. The guard claims they didn't load the weapon.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian pump-action shotgun with aggressive, functional lines. The silhouette is distinctly industrial—no ornament, no flourish. Compact and purposeful, designed for the hand of a tired security officer at 0400 hours.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length: 96 cm | Barrel length: 47 cm | Receiver width: 5.2 cm | Magazine tube diameter: 3.8 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty but balanced. At 3.0 kg, it settles into the shoulder with authority—not feather-light, but manageable for eight-hour shifts. The aluminum receiver distributes weight evenly along the tube.
physical_description.primary_material: Machined 6061-T6 aluminum alloy receiver; chrome-lined 12-gauge steel barrel; synthetic polymer furniture (foregrip, stock, magazine tube cap)
physical_description.finish: Matte black anodized aluminum receiver with light wear showing silver-gray scratches at sharp edges. Chrome-lined barrel with slight patina from prolonged use—not polished, deliberately functional. Stock and foregrip show micro-abrasions from thousands of handling cycles.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: Flat black anodized aluminum and blued steel | Accents: Chrome highlights on barrel, muzzle brake, and magazine cap | Subtle gray wear-through at contact points
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured black polymer grip with pronounced checkering for wet-glove retention. Magazine tube cap is knurled steel for positive hand-purchase during rapid reloading.
distinctive_features: Simple shotgun-style iron sights—no Picatinny rail, no optics mounting
Stubby muzzle brake with three expansion ports—visible scorch marks from sustained fire
Tubular magazine with witness ports showing round count
Pump handle with aggressive serrations, worn smooth in the middle from repeated cycling
Safety lever positioned for ambidextrous operation
Minimal dust cover where receiver meets barrel—tight machining, no rattles
Stamped serial number on left receiver side, faded from handling
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: KANG-PETROV ARMS / KPS-12 'WORKBENCH' stamped in small sans-serif font on left side of receiver | Simple block-letter 'KPA' logo on magazine cap | Serial number plate inset flush into aluminum
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn but maintained. Cosmetic dings and scratches throughout—evidence of heavy institutional use. The barrel shows fouling residue; the stock has scuff marks and a faint outline where a sling swivel once sat. Not abused, but visibly honest work. Armorer's marks on the receiver: tiny scribed hash-marks indicating maintenance intervals.
